Mr Ishvinder Singh, Adv. for R-  (through VC)
 CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JASMEET SINGH  ORDER % 21.04.2023 Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
The application stands disposed of.

1. This is a petition seeking quashing of FIR No. 999/2020 dated 30.11.2020, under Sections 498-A/376-B/377/354-A/328/34 IPC, registered at Police Station - Rajouri Garden and consequential proceedings, if any, emanating therefrom.
2. It seems that the allegations in the FIR are predicated on a matrimonial issue which the respondent No.2/complainant had with her husband, petitioner No.1.

3. During the pendency of the proceedings, the parties have arrived at a settlement dated 12.12.2022, pursuant to which the dispute has been settled and the respondent No.2 has agreed to cooperate in quashing of the FIR.
4. The petitioners are present in Court and have been identified by their counsel, Mr Ajay Singh.

5. The respondent No.2 is also present in Court through video conferencing and has been identified by her counsel Mr Ishvinder Singh through video conferencing as well as by the Investigating Officer SI Mukesh Yadadv, PS-Rajouri Garden.

sentences.text: Both the parties state that they have entered into the aforesaid settlement out of their own free will, volition and without any threat, force, undue influence or coercion.
It is stated by respondent No.2 that she wants to move on in her life and prays for quashing of the FIR.

It is stated that the second motion for divorce by mutual consent is now listed on 15.05.2023 before the Family Court,
Tis Hazari Court.
7. Mr Singh, learned APP states that the allegations in the FIR are under Sections 376-B/377 IPC and therefore, the FIR should not be quashed.
8. In the present case, the allegations have stemmed from a matrimonial dispute.
Once respondent No.2 has made a statement that she does not want to prosecute the FIR any further, I am of the view that no useful purpose would be served by prosecuting the case any further.
There is no child born out of the wedlock.

9. Since the parties have arrived at a settlement and no disputes are pending, I am convinced that quashing of such proceedings on account of compromise would bring about peace and would secure ends of justice.
This should not be treated as a legal precedent and in this case the proceedings are quashed as the respondent has decided to put a quietus to the matter.
The Court does not see any fruitful purpose if criminal proceedings are permitted to be prosecuted any further.
It is a fit case for quashing.
In this view of the matter, there is no reason to continue the proceedings.
10. However, I am of the view that considerable time of the police and judicial time has been wasted as the FIR is of the year 2020 and charge- sheet has been filed.

The police machinery has been put in motion on account of the acts of commission & omission on behalf of the parties and useful time of the police which could have been utilised for important matters has been misdirected towards this case.
Hence, the petitioner must pay some costs.

11. For the reasons stated above, FIR No. 999/2020 dated 30.11.2020, under Sections 498-A/376-B/377/354-A/328/34 IPC, registered at Police Station - Rajouri Garden and consequential proceedings, if any, emanating therefrom are hereby quashed subject to payment of costs of Rs. 10,000/- by the petitioners jointly to the Delhi Police Welfare Society Fund within a period of four weeks from today.
The proof of payment of cost shall be filed in the Registry within 4 weeks and in case the same is not furnished, this file be put up before the Court.
12. The petition is disposed of accordingly.
